Rupa Is a Sophisticated Camper Van With an Open Layout, Interior Staircase, and a Rooftop Terrace
30 photos
Photo: VannyCampers
For many vanlifers, camper vans are much more than just a mode of transportation. They are true homes on wheels, and as van conversions like the Rupa showcase, they can offer both beautiful aesthetics and modern functionality.
Luckily, there are countless ways to transform standard vans into genuine mobile dwellings, but making the most of the limited space available inside these vehicles often comes down to good design and clever organization rather than adding more features. This is also the design philosophy behind Rupa, and the result is a stunning roving home with an open interior layout, a soft color palette, and practical amenities that make everyday living on the road feel more like being at home.
This gorgeous camper van is based on a 2023 Mercedes-Benz Sprinter LWB with rear-wheel drive and a 2.0 CDI diesel engine. It’s a build designed for weekend getaways, coastal drives, road trips, and paved-road van life, and it stands out with its earth-toned, retro-inspired color palette and a unique interior arrangement that strays away from the popular side kitchen and rear fixed bed configuration.
Apart from that, the camper van incorporates some features that you don’t usually find in converted vehicles, such as an ingenious interior staircase, a rooftop terrace, and a walk-through bathroom. I’ll give you more details about each of them below.
Photo: VannyCampers But first, let’s talk about the choice of colors and finishes in this camper van. Named after the Sanskrit word for beauty and form, Rupa is one of those vans that look and feel like a luxurious hotel room. The interior styling combines understated neutrals with light terracotta/muted pink and green accents to create a cozy and highly sophisticated ambiance .
The star of the space is the Folly Pink shade, a warm, clay-like pink used on the lower cabinetry, the staircase, the framing of the shelving, and the accent walls. It brings a mid-century modern warmth to the space and combines with satin brass fixtures that add another tinge of luxury.
Most of the upper walls, the ceiling, and the upper cabinetry are finished in a soft, warm off-white that keeps the interior bright, airy, and spacious, without feeling sterile. Bespoke light green upholstery, an oak-effect flooring, and white stone-like countertops complete the interior design. Overall, the compact living space feels luxurious, relaxed, and full of character.
Photo: VannyCampers The rather uncommon layout showcases efficient use of space. There is no fixed partition wall between the driver’s cabin and the actual living area, and the double passenger seat swivels to provide extra seating at camp. At the front, a four-seater built-in sofa constitutes the lounge area, the central section of the van is occupied by a dual-sided kitchen, and at the rear, there is a walk-through wet bathroom.
When it comes to sleeping arrangements, Rupa can accommodate up to four travelers thanks to the convertible sofa that transforms into an extra-long bed measuring 189 x 137 cm (74 x 54 inches) and an additional bed in the pop-top. A removable table is also included. It can be mounted in front of the sofa to provide a practical space for dining or working on the road.
The distinct functional areas seamlessly flow into each other, and overhead storage integrated throughout the van makes it easy to keep personal belongings organized and the living space uncluttered.
Photo: VannyCampers One of the most eye-catching features inside Rupa is the staircase leading from the living area to the roof terrace. Rather than standing as a separate staircase, it seamlessly integrates into the kitchen design, providing additional storage. It’s also finished in the same shade of pink as the cabinetry, so it blends in perfectly.
This staircase leads to a hatch that opens onto the pop-top roof. This mezzanine area houses a 200-by-118-cm (79-by-46-inch) bed, perfect for one or two children. It comes with a panoramic canvas with zip-up windows and fly screens for proper ventilation.
Adjacent to it is another standout feature - a wooden roof deck that offers a nice, elevated place to spend time outside and take in the surrounding views.
Photo: VannyCampers Returning inside, the kitchen is quite spacious for a camper van . The dual-sided layout means there is ample counter space for meal prep, while modern appliances ensure modern functionality. The cooking equipment consists of a two-burner induction stove and a microwave, and the van is also equipped with a sink and a 58-liter Alpicool compressor fridge. A Truma D4E system provides hot water.
The rear bathroom is separated from the rest of the living area through a sliding door and is fitted with two white shower screens, stone-effect wall finishes, and a black mixer shower. A small matching sink and a Thetford 565 toilet are also included in this space for added convenience.
Photo: VannyCampers Though this camper van is not intended for adventurous off-road journeys, it does allow for extended trips away from the city or campsites. It is equipped with a 628Ah lithium battery bank that works in conjunction with 300W of solar panels on the roof and a 3,000W Renogy inverter charger. An external electrical hookup is also included. The electrical system components are housed in a dedicated compartment next to the rear bathroom, and garage storage is available above it.
Commissioned by VannyCampers in the UK, the Rupa is the next camper van set to be raffled off by the Bristol-based team, so if you’re feeling lucky, go buy some tickets for their online competition.
